name: Construction & Engineering
one_liner: Construction and engineering firms design and build buildings and infrastructure on a project basis, earning thin margins where bidding, execution risk and labor productivity decide profitability.
how_it_makes_money: Contractors win projects through competitive bids or negotiated contracts, paid under fixed-price, cost-plus, guaranteed-maximum-price or unit-rate terms. Engineering and design firms earn fees on professional services, and materials and equipment suppliers sell into projects.
revenue_formula: Revenue = backlog converted × project value recognized per period
New revenue = bids submitted × win rate × average contract value
Project margin = contract price - (labor + materials + subcontractors + equipment + overhead) ± change orders
cost_structure: Materials: steel, concrete, lumber and components, exposed to price swings
Labor: direct craft labor, often constrained by skilled-worker shortages
Subcontractors: specialty trades that perform much of the work on general contractor projects
Overhead, insurance and bonding: project management, safety, surety bonds
margins: General contractors often earn thin net margins in the low single digits, while specialty contractors, engineering firms and materials producers can earn more; fixed-price risk, cost overruns and labor productivity drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: Backlog
key_metrics.what: Contracted work not yet completed; the main indicator of future revenue.

key_metrics.name: Book-to-bill ratio
key_metrics.what: New orders relative to revenue; above 1 means backlog is growing.

key_metrics.name: Bid win rate
key_metrics.what: Share of bids won; reflects pricing and competitive positioning.

key_metrics.name: Gross margin by project
key_metrics.what: Project profitability after direct costs; shows execution quality.

key_metrics.name: Change order rate
key_metrics.what: Scope changes as a share of contract value; can protect or erode margin.

key_metrics.name: Schedule and cost variance
key_metrics.what: Deviation from planned timeline and budget; signals execution risk.

key_metrics.name: Safety incident rate (TRIR)
key_metrics.what: Recordable incidents per hours worked; affects cost, insurance and bid eligibility.

trends: Infrastructure spending from federal programs supporting public works backlog
Boom in data center, power grid and manufacturing plant construction
Skilled labor shortages and wage pressure
Materials cost volatility and tariffs affecting bids and margins
Adoption of prefabrication, modular construction and digital tools like BIM
Softer office and some commercial construction amid higher rates

case_angles.question: A general contractor is growing revenue but losing money. Why?

A construction firm's projects routinely run late. How do you fix operations?

interview_hooks: Why has construction productivity lagged other industries, and can modular building fix it?
Who should bear cost-overrun risk on large infrastructure projects?
Can the industry meet the data center and grid build-out given labor constraints?
